algeria: Compact rock towers differ in silhouette/spacing; warmer streaked wood and simpler brass. Open rear attachment looks separated; hinge clarity hold, not proven detachment.
australia: Five domes retained but smoother/more regular; finer repetitive sandstone stripes versus broad irregular promotional bands. Open hinge connection ambiguous.
belgium: Fossil stone reads densely speckled versus individual promotional rings; branching relief more angular, brass flatter. Open hinge connection ambiguous.
brunei: Saturated burgundy and dense regular diamonds versus muted tactile promotional brocade; raised-thread impression weaker. Open lid appears floating but discrete hinge contact is unresolved, not proven absent.
central-african-republic: Smooth lobed trees, flatter clearing/water and simpler wood/stone versus detailed foliage. Open rear hinge connection visually ambiguous.
croatia: Three pools retained but compact regular basins and simplified spillways; smoother ivory stone and uniform water. Open hinge/lid interface visually ambiguous.
dr-congo: Rounded canopy and winding river retained; marketing foliage fuller and raffia diamonds bolder. Original confirms feet and side ring are present despite board-scale ambiguity.
ethiopia: Three plateau forms retained; viewer cliffs more faceted, stone diagonals more repetitive on open underside. Marketing adds relief and shading.
ghana: Marketing has conspicuous raised rectangular brass lid handle; actual closed viewer has only a small flat-looking central ornament. Graphic textile and regular wood bands versus tactile promotional finish.
honduras: Two tree clusters, pale angular terrain and winding river retained; lid darker green than marketing mint/jade and foliage more faceted. Major hardware present.
ireland: Marketing side ring reads larger/heavier; actual masonry is smaller/tidier and marble broad cream waves rather than fine green contour layering.
kiribati: Interrupted lagoon shore and curled/sloping segment confirmed in original; regular flat weave and simpler vegetation shading versus promotion.
libya: Arch and pale lid inset retained; actual ochre more saturated, stone angular and strongly mottled/striated versus softer promotion.
mali: Three formations retain arrangement; faceted stacked ledges and golden mottling versus rounded gullies and muted sand. Exact summit proportions not certified.
monaco: Marketing village occupies larger footprint on taller irregular stepped cliff; actual compact cluster on lower regular shelf exposes more blue lid.
nepal: Originals confirm three separate snowcapped peaks on flat exposed lid, not a missing connected range. Actual banding graphic, snow brighter and contact shadows weaker.
norway: Two mountain masses frame the fjord consistently. Actual cyan water flatter, slopes faceted and body bands regular versus stronger promotional depth.
paraguay: Radial ivory lace and hardware retained; actual pink wood brighter with stronger bands, lace less resolved at small scale. Full historical archive inventory remains separately unchecked.
russia: Ice blocks and fracture identity retained; actual flatter polygonal blocks and graphic fractures versus sculpted ice and nuanced blue grain.
saudi-arabia: Three sandstone formations retain arrangement; regular stacked bands and wood-grain-like striations versus eroded granular promotional rock.
solomon-islands: Subdued charcoal/gray ebony in marketing versus warm reddish-brown body and lighter tan lid in viewer; conspicuous repetitive grain and flatter inlays.
sudan: Three-pyramid composition retained; less evident masonry and sand relief, brighter broad ochre mottling versus muted granular sandstone.
the-moon: Principal crater/highlands retained; smoother rims/ridges and cloudy pale texture versus richer sculpted mineral relief. Hardware simpler.
tuvalu: Marketing broader irregular sand landform versus compact low faceted enclosing platform and elongated irregular turquoise oval in actual viewer; weave flatter/more regular.
vanuatu: Raised recessed volcano retained but faceted; nearly uniform pale orange-yellow ember patch versus richly patterned molten promotional material, coarser ash mottling.
